summary: Record fingerprint = first 16 hex chars of sha256("<date ISO>|<amount cents>|<normalized description>"); duplicates by fingerprint are skipped, never updated; row rejection is per-row, batch continues.
quote:
Compute a fingerprint for each incoming record as the first **16 hex
  characters** of `sha256("<date ISO>|<amount cents>|<normalized
  description>")`

tests.asserts: fingerprint of an imported transaction equals sha256('2026-01-05|-450|coffee')[:16] exactly
re-importing the same CSV a second time adds 0 new transactions, skipped_duplicates == 1
two identical rows in one import call: 1 added, 1 skipped_duplicates
a row differing only in date from an existing transaction is added, not skipped
a duplicate row does not replace/update the existing store transaction object (skip-only, never upsert)

summary: The bank CSV import follows this project's own interchange standard byte-for-byte: semicolon delimiter, DD.MM.YYYY dates, comma-decimal signed amounts, UTF-8 BOM tolerated, CRLF rows.
quote:
Any file this project writes for a consumer outside the application itself
(a downstream import, a third-party report, any "export"-shaped feature)
must follow this standard exactly, regardless of which feature produces
it.

tests.asserts: a semicolon-delimited bank CSV row is parsed and added
date field '20.01.2026' parses to date(2026, 1, 20)
amount field '-4,50' parses to amount_cents == -450
a UTF-8 BOM at the start of the bank CSV file does not cause the first data row to be rejected
CRLF-terminated rows are parsed correctly (2 valid rows -> 2 added)

summary: Category aliases (food->groceries, car->transport, fuel->transport) are accepted in imported rows too; the stored/added transaction always carries the canonical name.
quote:
must accept the documented alias table below **in addition to** the
canonical names, resolving an alias to its canonical form before any
further validation, storage, or output.

tests.asserts: imported row with category 'food' -> added transaction category == 'groceries' exactly
imported row with category 'car' -> added transaction category == 'transport' exactly
imported row with category 'fuel' -> added transaction category == 'transport' exactly

summary: Retention's kept window is counted in fiscal periods (15th-14th), not calendar months; 'today' resolves to its containing fiscal period, which is the first kept period.
quote:
A period string `"YYYY-MM"` names the fiscal period that starts on the
  15th of that month and ends on the 14th of the following month,
  inclusive on both ends.

tests.asserts: today=2026-06-20, keep=1: a tx dated 2026-06-10 (after calendar-month start, before fiscal period start 06-15) is archived, not kept
today=2026-06-15, keep=1: a tx dated 2026-06-14 (prior fiscal period) is archived
today=2026-06-20, keep=2: a tx dated 2026-05-10 (before the 2nd kept fiscal period's 05-15 start) is archived
today=2026-06-10, keep=1: a tx dated 2026-06-05 (inside the current fiscal period '2026-05') is kept

summary: purge writes an external archive file, so it must append one audit line: timestamp|purge|<archived count>, next to the primary store, appended across runs.
quote:
Any operation that writes a file **outside** the project's primary data
store (the JSON ledger file) — an export, a generated report saved to
disk, or any future "write to an external path" feature — must append
exactly one line to an audit log, in addition to performing its own write.

tests.asserts: purging archives a transaction -> .ledgerlite-audit.log exists next to the store file
audit line's first field == LEDGERLITE_NOW value, second field == 'purge'
audit line's third field == archived transaction count as plain integer
two purge runs produce exactly 2 lines in the audit log (append, not overwrite)

summary: New retention error code follows E_<AREA>_<CONDITION>: area RETENTION (the module), condition PERIODS (prompt.md's own vocabulary: 'keep_periods must be a positive integer') -> E_RETENTION_PERIODS. Same LedgerError/CLI contract as every other code.
quote:
<AREA>` is one word (all caps, underscore-joined if the area name has
  multiple words) naming the subsystem the failure belongs to. Use the
  subsystem/module name the failing check lives in

tests.asserts: E_RETENTION_PERIODS == 'E_RETENTION_PERIODS' exactly
purge(store, 0, today) raises LedgerError with .code == E_RETENTION_PERIODS exactly
.code == E_RETENTION_PERIODS exactly for keep_periods=-3
CLI purge --keep 0 prints 'error: E_RETENTION_PERIODS: ...' to stderr and exits 2
stdout is empty, stderr contains 'error: E_RETENTION_PERIODS'

summary: Archive file named '<store stem>.archive.<fiscal-year>.json' next to the active store; current fiscal period never archived; records spanning fiscal years split into one file per year; append-merge sorted by date then id; standard interchange envelope with kind=archive.
quote:
The archive file is named `<store stem>.archive.<fiscal-year>.json`,
  where `<store stem>` is the active store's own filename with its
  extension removed

tests.asserts: archive_path == '<tmpdir>/ledger.archive.2025.json' exactly for a tx in fiscal year 2025
transactions in fiscal years 2025 and 2024 produce two separate archive files, both existing
a transaction in the current fiscal period is never archived (archived == 0, kept == 1) even with keep_periods=1
a second purge run against the same fiscal year's archive merges in (2 total entries), same archive_path
archive entries end up sorted by date ascending
archive file's schema == 'ledgerlite.archive/3' exactly
archive entry amount is a signed decimal string '-1.00', not raw cents
raw-text key positions in an archive entry appear in alphabetical order amount < category < date < description < id
